purpose: clean the tiktok user data and visualize the data

```{r}
# Downloading dataset
if (!requireNamespace("here", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("here"); 
library(here)

file_path <- here("data", "raw", "users.csv")
if (!dir.exists(dirname(file_path))) {
  dir.create(dirname(file_path), recursive = TRUE)
}
data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hannesdatta/course-dprep/refs/heads/main/material/project/coaching_2_data/users.csv"
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  download.file(data_url, destfile = file_path, mode = "wb")
  message("Dataset successfully downloaded to: ", file_path)
} else {
  message("Dataset already exists in: ", file_path, ". Skipping download.")
}

# Naming dataset 
users <- read.csv(file_path)

#Install packages 
required_packages <- c("here", "ggplot2", "glue")
install.packages(setdiff(required_packages, rownames(installed.packages())))

# Loading packages
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
library(glue)
```

## Cleaning the data 
```{r}
# Inspect data
head(users)
names(users)
str(users)
summary(users)

# Remove missing values
colSums(is.na(users))
sum(!complete.cases(users))
users_clean <- na.omit(users)
dim(users)
dim(users_clean)
colSums(is.na(users_clean))
```

## Making of plots 

```{r}
# Create plot
histogram_users<- ggplot(users_clean, aes(x = base_videos_watched_mean)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(fill = after_stat(count)),
    bins = 30,
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#dfeaf4",
    high = "#1f3b75",
    name = "Count"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Average Videos Watched",
    x = "Average videos watched per user",
    y = "Number of users"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

  # Save plot
  file_path_merge<- here("gen", "output", "users_analysis")
    if (!dir.exists(dirname(file_path_merge))) {
  dir.create(dirname(file_path_merge), recursive = TRUE)
}

plot_filename<- glue("average_videos_watched_distribution_{Sys.Date()}.png")

ggsave(
  filename=here("gen", "output", "users_analysis", plot_filename), plot= histogram_users,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)


```
